notes.title: Ars Notoria Journal #8
notes.content:
Hi, everyone!

In this development log, we wanted to share with you various gameplay updates and new features that we prepared for the testing build of the game. We have finished developing all planned content for the build and are now doing final balancing and optimizations. There are many new additions to all gameplay systems, from combat and skills to building and crafting.

Harvesting skills

One of the biggest new additions to the game are the 9 skill trees dedicated to harvesting professions. Each skill tree consists of 12 nodes that provide unique bonuses to the related profession. Characters can gain experience and level up these skills when gathering resources using the corresponding tools.

https://i.imgur.com/LKy5FRO.gif

New harvesting skills include:

 Woodcutting - allows collecting different types of wood using lumberjack axes, as well as providing bonuses for finding special woods and regrowing trees.
 Mining - determines how good characters are at harvesting ores, allows splitting ore deposits faster, and helps find rare types of ores.
 Quarrying - helps harvest stone blocks and split stone deposits with a sledgehammer more efficiently, and provides some unique features, such as blast mining.
 Digging - allows excavating various resources, such as clay, from the ground. It also provides a useful side bonus that helps find hidden treasures.
 Hoeing - a skill that improves the harvesting of resources like pigments from deposits on the ground.
 Splitting - this skill allows gathering salts from deposits using specialized iron bars. It also helps to find rare gemstones while splitting mineral deposits.
 Farming - a useful skill that provides various bonuses for growing and harvesting crops, as well as raising farm animals.
 Reaping - measures how efficiently characters can grow various plant fibers (like cotton or flax) and then gather them using a sickle.
 Gathering - helps characters collect various medicinal herbs and other ingredients needed for crafting potions, tinctures, poisons, etc.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42814198/a7736410966d056e1c29954e810abeac1def65ce.png
Together with the harvesting skills, there are dozens of new craftable items for harvesting, processing, and storing resources. They are designed to work together with the harvesting skills and help optimize or, in later stages of the game walkthrough, automate the harvesting process.

Taming

Another significant addition to the game is the taming system. It was requested on our socials quite often, and we also think that it’s a great feature that can improve the overall gameplay. Now characters can tame any type of wild animal (such as a wolf, boar, deer, fox, etc.) that is present in the game.

https://i.imgur.com/paaiBdD.gif

There is an Affection meter for each animal, which determines whether an animal is hostile, neutral, or friendly toward the player’s character. It can be raised by giving them food (all animals have different preferences, and offering them their favorite food makes the taming process faster) or by petting them once they become friendly.

https://i.imgur.com/Te7pTHS.gif

There are 10 Affection levels in total, each one offering various bonuses and changing the behavior of an animal. The first few levels reduce the animal’s aggressiveness and allow characters to walk closer without being attacked. After the third level, the animal becomes neutral and won’t attack the player anymore unless it receives direct damage. It also allows characters to approach the animal and pet it to further increase Affection. Higher levels of Affection make animals friendly to the player, allowing to name them, as well as give various commands such as following the character or guarding territories.

New animal types

With the addition of the taming system, we also expanded the number of wild and domesticated animals present in the game. Now there are 11 types of animals that are either domesticated by default or can be tamed: cows, sheep, goats, pigs, chickens, wolves, foxes, boars, deer, bears, and rats.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42814198/944426d79036db8e06ed32dae6ab2a34b0b35623.png
Raising or taming animals can provide access to valuable resources such as hides, wool, milk, eggs, meat, etc. We also integrated taming and new animal types with the updated Farming profession. There are various tools to process the obtained resources (such as a tanning rack, for example) and equipment that helps to take care of the animals (barns, fences, feeders).

Cooking

Together with the farming system, we implemented the cooking system and significantly expanded the number of available ingredients and types of food. Now there are more than 200 ingredients and recipes in the game.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42814198/89359353b5553496422cef82045ce229fda211f7.png
Each type of food or recipe provides various useful bonuses to characters (such as temporarily raising stats or attributes, resistances, regeneration speed, etc.) and helps to prepare for exploration and battles. There are no hunger or thirst meters by default, and no negative effects for not consuming food, so it’s totally up to players whether to use it (we might add an optional setting to the server menu for those who would prefer to have such functionality, though).

https://i.imgur.com/WXofV3r.gif

Each type of craftable equipment for cooking (campfire, cooking pot, oven) has from one to five slots for cooking ingredients. A higher number of ingredient slots allows the preparation of more complicated recipes that provide stronger bonuses. New recipes can be discovered either by experimenting with various ingredients or by finding them in the open world.

Diseases and status effects

We also added different types of diseases, each with multiple stages and unique gameplay effects, and new status effects to the game. They are integrated with other systems (such as weather, food, or enemies) and have certain conditions that cause them. For example, prolonged exposure to cold or heat without appropriate gear or resistance can cause Frostbite or Heatstroke.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42814198/3c522bdd8708455a640e01cb03ab1ed9a6704f3d.png
When left untreated for a long time, diseases can progress to more advanced stages, inflicting various negative effects. But they can be treated with craftable remedies by Herbalists and Apothecaries or, in some cases, by simply stopping exposure to harmful effects.

https://i.imgur.com/rKy31wL.gif

To implement diseases, we also updated various in-game mechanics, such as temperature and weather effects. All world zones now have a dynamic temperature that is affected by time of day, season, weather, and heat sources. Craftable items like campfires, torches, or braziers provide heat in a certain radius around them and can help prevent status effects like chilling, freezing, or wetness.

Climbing

Another new feature introduced to the game is climbing. We had it implemented for some time as an experimental feature, but with further testing and improvements, we decided that it was ready to be added to the game. The climbing system is fully dynamic and is supported by almost all surfaces and objects (cliffs, walls, trees, buildings).

https://i.imgur.com/KpjRo1Z.gif

Climbing provides access to otherwise unreachable places and also helps to improve the traversal of the open world. It also supports jumping, which can speed up the climbing process or allow for overcoming obstacles.

Building mode updates

With the addition of new harvesting equipment, building parts, and other craftable items, we decided that the building menu needed an overhaul for easier navigation and categorization of buildable objects. The building menu consists of 6 large parts: Construction, Encampment, Harvesting, Production, Farming, and Furniture. Then, each of them is divided into 9 categories for individual objects. For example, the Encampment tab consists of categories like Campfires, Tents, Defenses, Fortifications, Weapon Stands, Training Equipment, Banners, Bags, and Blankets. And each category has various craftable items related to it.

https://i.imgur.com/oE8rAfO.gif

We also added an option to easily switch the tier of craftable items (Common, Uncommon, Rare) inside the building menu by clicking on the selector above it or using hotkeys (the mouse wheel in the case of using a mouse and keyboard setup). And we implemented advanced tooltips that can be optionally toggled to display detailed parameters and bonuses for buildable objects.

Building customization

We fully finished the building customization system introduced a bit earlier and greatly expanded the number of options available for customization. Now it is possible to customize the majority of buildable objects as long as they have surfaces that can be painted (such as fabric or wood).

https://i.imgur.com/YuK3gJN.gif

The customization system allows changing the object’s colors, applying patterns and images, adjusting their scale, position, and rotation, as well as saving and loading created styles. We have added many new types of patterns and images that can be painted on craftable objects. For example, you can create custom banners and flags for your faction or completely change the look of encampments, buildings, and other objects.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42814198/ce7c47b214858c224d5987ae62c8c60bc195294e.png
Building bonuses and interactions

Apart from customization options, we also added various gameplay bonuses and interactions for most of the building parts. They can be used for resting, storing items, training, displaying trophies, providing heat and light, etc. Each object has parameters like Decor, Comfort, Durability, and can provide some special bonuses to characters. Many of the buildable objects also grant access to other gameplay systems like cooking, harvesting, and production.

https://i.imgur.com/GsCk6KN.gif

Decor and comfort values provide bonuses to different status effects (like the Well Rested effect), improve regeneration speed while resting, and grant other benefits (for example, Decor value can make selling items at the shops that you build more profitable).

Combat mode updates

We also made a lot of tweaks and updates to the combat system in the game. We have added a new UI panel that displays available combat moves and abilities in more detail, implemented demonstrations for skills in the tooltips, and added new default abilities. Furthermore, we also added Unarmed attacks and skills (which doesn’t count as a separate skill tree but can be useful at the beginning stages of the game).

https://i.imgur.com/vowhsAr.gif

An important part of the combat system is physical and elemental effects, as well as their combinations. There are four physical damage types and resistances (Slashing, Crushing, Piercing, Ballistic), and six elemental ones (Fire, Frost, Poison, Lightning, Chaos, and Holy). By inflicting damage of a certain type on enemies, you can build up various effects that can immobilize them, make them weaker, or deal damage over time. Different effects can also be combined into more powerful ones and provide additional advantages over enemies. Applying physical and elemental effects to the enemies also improves the effectiveness of the characters' strong attacks and makes them significantly more deadly.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42814198/bd6ea3a341218516aec3f8497f46cf1ab20d544c.png
There are also some quality-of-life features for the combat system, such as training dummies and shooting targets that allow to measure damage of different attacks, DPS of combo attacks, and effect buildups.


That’s it for today’s development log update. There are many smaller additions and tweaks that we made in preparation for the testing build. We will try to cover them in future logs, but now the main priority is to make sure that the testing build is fully ready for the launch and that all the new content works correctly. We are trying to finish the last balancing passes and optimizations as fast as we can, but it’s important to do them properly in order to significantly reduce the number of potential issues during the launch of the testing. We are very thankful to all of you for your patience!

notes.title: Ars Notoria Journal #7
notes.content:
Hi everyone!

We are working hard to prepare everything for the closed testing of the game, and we have recently made some improvements to the building and crafting system that we wanted to share with you.

There are a total of 9 harvesting and 9 crafting professions in the game. Harvesting professions focus on collecting various types of resources (such as wood, stone, and iron) and then processing them into more advanced materials (lumber, stone blocks, and iron ingots). Crafting professions allow using these materials to create new items and equipment. In one of the previous development logs, we covered crafting professions in more detail. Here is the link if you want to check them out: Ars Notoria Journal #4

Previously, harvesting professions were much more simplified than crafting ones. They had less equipment available, no harvesting skills or abilities, and the progression was quite limited (only rarity tiers for equipment and resources). However, since collecting resources is an important mechanic during all game stages, especially in the beginning, we decided that making them fully functional professions instead of simplified ones would be a significant improvement.

Harvesting equipment

We have added new types of equipment for each harvesting profession and organized them according to their functionality and bonuses. Here is an example of a lumberjack’s tools and the order in which they are unlocked.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42814198/ee737709f45d3ed3c26ba856d9a0f400f5e3cf10.png

The lumberjack’s equipment can be divided into two main groups: the first group is tools for harvesting and processing wood, and the second group is equipment for trading. This way, you can set up dedicated lumberjack workshops that can help you collect wood and obtain more advanced materials from it, as well as selling excess resources if needed.


 Axe - a basic tool that allows you to cut down trees more efficiently. You can unlock it right from the start of the game by acquiring some wood, and it can be crafted directly from your inventory.

https://i.imgur.com/P5nXANo.gif
 Log Storage - increases the available global storage for wood. Resources don’t use the same inventory as normal items (like armor, swords, or consumables), and there is separate global storage for them accessible anywhere. By building expansions like Log Storage, you can increase the size of storage available for the specific resource.

https://i.imgur.com/OlCpG0s.gif
 Circular Saw - an instrument that allows processing wood into lumber. You can load wood into it, and after some time, it will be converted into lumber automatically.

https://i.imgur.com/B7xQaek.gif
 Lumber Storage - increases the available global storage for lumber.

https://i.imgur.com/pRwtsNL.gif
 Tar Kiln - a kiln that can produce tar from wood. It works in a similar manner as Circular Saw and will automatically convert all the wood that you put into it to tar.

https://i.imgur.com/lX36hXT.gif
 Tar Storage - increases the available global storage for tar.

https://i.imgur.com/Daoli6H.gif
 Debarker - a tool that increases the wood processing speed of nearby Circular Saw and/or Tar Kiln and can also automatically load resources from the global storage (after the specified threshold) and put them into corresponding instruments. After resource processing finishes, it also transfers obtained materials to the global storage.

https://i.imgur.com/v9hYyCk.gif
 Sawmill - a large machine that helps to harvest logs. Its efficiency depends on the number of trees within its range, and it will regularly provide you with extra wood logs.

https://i.imgur.com/u4dlPIZ.gif
 Workbench - allows assigning workers to collect wood for you. Their harvesting speed depends on the tools they are equipped with (better quality axes will allow collecting more wood) and their skill level.
 Counter - a place where you can assign a worker to sell excess wood, lumber, or tar for you.
 Stand - allows displaying resources for sale and increases the selling speed.
 Platform - storage where you can put materials for selling or specify a threshold for each resource after which it will be put on sale automatically.
 Sign - provides various bonuses to selling resources.

Most of the lumberjack’s tools aim to increase the efficiency of collecting wood and automation of this process, but it’s also important to make sure that manual resource harvesting doesn’t become devalued and less relevant. There are certain mechanics to prevent this. Only basic crafting resources can be obtained this way (81 resources in total divided between 9 harvesting professions), and unique resources (142 resources in total) still need to be collected by the characters manually. Basic crafting resources are usually used in large quantities for building and crafting (for example, when constructing fortified bases/outposts or settlements), and having various workshops to help with their harvesting can make it less tedious. At the same time, unique resources are pretty rare and usually hidden in more dangerous places, so gathering them manually while exploring the game region with your combat squad is more common. Overall, we want to make harvesting equipment a nice addition to the process of collecting resources, but not a complete replacement for manual harvesting.

Harvesting skills

Other new additions to the harvesting professions are skills. Previously, only crafting professions had dedicated skill trees, and we felt that harvesting professions were missing some kind of progression. So we decided to implement harvesting skills as well. Here is an example of a woodcutting skill tree.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42814198/c7a830da389e86d3045c92e57a58da3eaa35d411.png

The skill trees have different branches that focus on various areas of the resource gathering process. Some provide bonuses to harvesting speed or quantity of obtained resources, while others grant more unique abilities, like allowing you to plant trees for woodcutting or increasing their growth speed. The skills are designed to work together with harvesting equipment and complement it. For example, you can plant trees within the range of the sawmill to improve its efficiency, or obtain an ability that increases the amount of harvested unique resources, which is not possible to achieve with only harvesting tools. Workers who can be assigned to help you with resource gathering also benefit from improving their skills, and their efficiency depends on their skill level.

There are also various quality-of-life improvements regarding the building menu and its user interface. We added the ability to switch between equipment rarity levels directly in the menu, added indicators for missing resources and locked tools, as well as refined the process of auto-alignment of building parts to the terrain.

That’s it for today’s update. Thank you so much for checking it out!

notes.title: Ars Notoria Journal #6
notes.content:
Hi, everyone!

In this development log update, we wanted to share with you some new building features that we recently added to the game. They mostly include various interior objects, decorations, and mechanics that will allow you to further customize your buildings.

[previewyoutube=fxXg5GPZEqw;full][/previewyoutube]

There are many new furniture objects and decorations that you can place inside buildings that you constructed: from tables, chairs, fireplaces, shelves, cupboards, and cabinets to curtains, rugs, paintings, chandeliers, and tableware.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42814198/e8c4179ca482e6cbe0ab7a3e58b7f091d12366a3.png

Patterns

https://i.imgur.com/42GewJN.gif

We added a new customization option that allows you to apply various patterns to building elements and adjust all of their parameters (color, scale, rotation, offset). For example, you can choose a texture that will be applied to a wooden wall panel, change the colors of different parts of the panel (wood, pattern main and background colors), as well as modify its size or position.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42814198/9ad8580422f9fd0066e03c5420beaca5c92cb75f.png

Designs that you create can also be saved, so you can reuse them later, and it’s also possible to apply them automatically to all building elements of the same type in the room.

Trophies

https://i.imgur.com/G5zvaAb.gif

Another feature that we implemented recently is trophies. You will be able to obtain them after defeating various enemies and bosses, and also as rewards for completing certain quests. We added special craftable stands and wall mounts where you can place them.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42814198/59e3e8e342abcc6d74ff0899c91b95ab39d0ab44.png

Armor and weapon stands

https://i.imgur.com/F58COhG.gif

Together with stands for trophies, we added different types of craftable armor and weapon stands. You will be able to display various armor pieces, weapons, and artifacts that you obtained while exploring the game world on these stands. They have several types like free-standing or wall-mounted, as well as weapon cabinets.

Spiral staircases

https://i.imgur.com/7mSG5IH.gif

We also added modules for creating spiral staircases (stairs, railings, and special floor pieces). Multiple spiral staircase modules can be connected together in case you want to use them for multi-floor towers or other tall structures. They are much more compact than normal stairs and can fit into a single modular floor piece, so they can be also useful for small buildings where there isn’t much space available.

Greenhouses

https://i.imgur.com/Ci56E43.gif

There are some new furniture objects for gardening and farming that can help you to create greenhouses or herbalist workshops: planters for crops, hanging racks, flower pots, gardener tables, containers for storing herbs, etc. Using this equipment you will be able to cultivate plants that you discover in the game world inside houses that you build.

Thank you so much for checking out this development blog post!

notes.title: Ars Notoria Journal #5
notes.content:
Hi, everyone!

We have added some new building parts and functionality to the building mode this past few weeks and wanted to share these updates with you.

[previewyoutube=RYsEp2CLrw4;full][/previewyoutube]
Here is a video demonstrating the use of new modules and how to construct more advanced buildings than we showed previously, in case you haven’t checked it already on our YouTube or Discord channels.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42814198/80a93d41c3f8e76bb103fb52f050098b7348086d.png

The new building parts include:

 Triangle foundations and floors. They are based on equilateral triangles with 2-meter sides and can be combined together with square foundations to create quite complicated shapes. We’ve added two levels for them: a wooden one for village houses and a stone one for city houses and other advanced buildings.
 Two new types of roofs. We added 45° roof modules and corresponding wall modules to support them which can be used to create most types of roofs for city houses, as well as 60° modules, which are the most useful for towers and other roofs that benefit from having a steep incline.
 Balconies, awnings, and columns. These parts can be used when creating multi-floor houses and making different types of porches and patios.
 Stair modules. We’ve added new parts for wooden and stone stairs that are sturdier than previous ones and can be combined together to build large staircases.
 Double doors and large windows. Previously we had parts for single doors and standard windows, so we decided to add a new wall module that supports double doors, and also the ability to install large windows on short walls (which can be quite useful for creating greenhouses, bay windows, etc).
 Fences and decorations. We also added iron fence modules and various types of decorations that you can use to improve the looks of houses that you build: flower pots and beds, statues, and a fountain.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42814198/445f26d47d09a6858d6cf5bab3b0c2cff172b971.png

Another new addition is the ability to select the material, color, and style of building parts. For example, you can choose between different types of stone, brick, and wood for stone wall elements, apply custom colors to them, and select the pattern you prefer. Materials, colors, and styles can be changed anytime both on new parts that you plan to place or already existing ones. There are also tools to automatically apply the selected style and colors to all adjacent parts of the same type, so you will be able to easily change the looks of the whole room or even the full house.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42814198/af0c6bea6805b36feb47928b3df3e4470f7d7a63.png

Styles are supported by most of the building modules (walls, floors, ceilings, roofs, windows, doors, etc) and furniture (tables, beds, chairs, and others). We’ve already added several types for each category (8 for walls, 4 for windows, 3 for doors, from 2 to 5 for various furniture pieces) and plan to continue increasing the variety in the future too.

In this article and the video we focused mostly on the exterior parts, but we are already preparing a second part that will feature making interiors and putting different workshops inside the building that we’ve built. 

Thank you a lot for checking out this part of our development blog!

notes.title: Ars Notoria Journal #4
notes.content:
Hey everyone!

In this part of our development blog, we wanted to share some details about the crafting system and various professions in Ars Notoria.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42814198/013ec933cf1b57065fa2c3602b8c559fd98e6848.png

There are various crafting professions available in the game, which characters can learn to create new items and make them stronger. Each one focuses on a specific area of crafting and unlocks unique item recipes. The professions include the following types:


 Alchemist - scholar that studies minerals and elements to combine them into dangerous explosives, acids, powders, or to create protective barriers.
 Weaponsmith - craftsman that can create all kinds of weapons from swords and polearms, to pistols and rifles.
 Armorer - artisan that specializes in crafting different types of armor (light, medium, and heavy) and defensive equipment like shields.
 Jeweler - master of producing magical accessories that can be used to cast spells and improve the strength of the user’s magic.
 Apothecary - healer that brews various potions, tinctures, elixirs, and also specialize in poisons and ways to neutralize them.
 Carpenter - expert in building any types of wooden constructions, equipment, and devices.
 Engineer - inventor that is able to build unique upgrades for existing equipment and tools to greatly improve their efficiency.
 Mason - builder that can create stone constructions of any complexity, raise stone walls, towers, and fortify the settlements.
 Merchant - tradesman who can bring exotic items and resources from different remote regions and also sell goods there.


{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42814198/93dc718507e7a2e85417256d691eb7d3a4fc1f9e.png

Each of the professions has its own crafting tools and equipment that are necessary to create items. For example, Weaposmith has access to Hammer, Bellows, Anvil, Rifling Machine, Polishing Wheel, and Forge. These tools allow to craft additional types of weapons and improve their quality. By using these crafting tools, Weaponsmiths are able to create Swords, Blunt Weapons, Polearms, Pistol, Rifles, and Hand Mortars.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42814198/f370fd7dc39860466a2864e14e8397a8e40b4669.png

Each piece of crafting equipment has three levels, and every level allows working with higher quality materials and unlocks more advanced items. It can be upgraded by using better resources that you can find while exploring the region’s territories. You can create new equipment from the building menu and place it anywhere you want: inside the houses that you’ve built, in dedicated workshops, or just outside in the temporary camp.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42814198/e8c4e36dff14156eadb6e8875670a8311fb370c3.png

Resources that are used for crafting can be divided into two main categories: basic and special. Basic resources include common materials like wood, stone, iron, leather, fabric, glass, and other types. They can be used in construction and also serve as a base ingredient for most of the craftable equipment. These materials are abundant throughout the region and are relatively easy to find. Raw materials that you find can also be processed into more advanced ones by using corresponding tools. For example, Iron Ore can be processed into Iron Ingots, Logs of Wood into Lumber, and Clay into Bricks or Ceramics.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42814198/f872023f7c23f93040e068df6a4b5b42e9726f05.png

Special resources include minerals, gemstones, elements, metal shards, rare types of wood and herbs, etc. They can be used to craft equipment and items with unique properties. For example, some uncommon materials can grant additional fire resistance to armor parts or can be used to add burning effects to weapons. Special resources are typically harder to find than basic ones, and they require expeditions to dungeon depths or remote deposits.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42814198/40a56f72aaab5617fc7ff8378d298bd3ae1c5081.png

Apart from the crafting equipment, another important feature of professions is Skills. Each profession has two related skill trees that can you can develop to make craftable items more powerful and grant them additional properties. By creating new items and using them in combat, you can level up the corresponding skills and unlock new abilities.

The skill trees for each profession are the following:

 Alchemy and Explosives for Alchemists
 Armament and Ballistics for Weaponsmiths
 Light Armor and Heavy Armor for Armorers
 Relics and Inlay for Jewelers
 Medicine and Toxicology for Apothecaries
 Supply and Coordination for Carpenters
 Engineering and Technology for Engineers
 Fortification and Organization for Masons
 Logistics and Navigation for Merchants


{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42814198/d6c099fa29318b013e442cf0ebb99f3b72925174.png

You can build your own workshops or acquire existing ones for all professions and use them to organize the production of items and their trade. It’s up to you if you prefer to craft everything yourself or entrust it to your faction members instead. They can be assigned to work in workshops and complete tasks like collecting and processing resources, crafting items, and either leaving them for you to use in combat or selling to the inhabitants of the region, providing an additional source of income for your faction. As time passes, the assigned craftsmen will perfect their skills and become able to craft higher-quality items with unique properties.

Thank you for checking out this development blog post! The crafting system in the game is quite complex, and it’s hard to explain all the details about it in a single article. We will continue to cover crafting in future articles, focusing more on individual professions, their crafting tools, resources, skills, and what types of items they produce.

notes.title: Festival of Souls
notes.content:
Greetings future Soul Hunters! Narrative Director Chad Briggs here to tell you all about the spooky season in the world of Ars Notoria! Given the game's multitude of beings possessed by dark spirit energy, this time of the year in our game world is both insanely fun and delightfully macabre. This is just one of the many seasons being implemented in pursuit of providing the player with tons of unique, seasonal activities and quests. But first, some basic information on the passage of time and our game seasons.

https://i.imgur.com/VikzboL.gif

As you’ve previously gotten a glimpse of in several gameplay clips and stills, the world of Ars Notoria has four distinct seasons. These seasons come and go with the natural passing of accelerated time based on our in-game calendar. The open-ended world allows the player the opportunity to experience many years and many seasons, as they are not tied to real-world dates/times.  These game seasons are: 

Ren - Season of Renewal (Spring)
Lux - Season of Light (Summer)
Aur - Season of Harvest (Fall)
Dim - Season of Twilight (Winter)

https://i.imgur.com/VXz0J7y.gif

One of the things we’ll talk about in a future blog post is the different classes of spirit magic, called Ars, that can be harnessed during the game.  For seven days per season in the game world, each Ars will have a moment to draw upon more spirit energy than normal, gaining an edge over the others. The first seven days of Aur, the Season of Harvest, favor the Ars Necromia, a magic with dark designs on chaos and necromancy.  

https://i.imgur.com/PO55upJ.gif

During this season, practitioners of this Ars are in full force, dabbling in occult forces, undead beings, and blood magic. These unnatural perversions of spirit magic will pit you against new, unique Enthralled that only show up during the seven zenith days of Aur, many hovering around tombs and cemeteries where the undead concentration is strongest. Of these creatures, few are more disturbing than the mutated, spider-pumpkin, an Enthralled being created from angry, vengeful spirits and dark Ars magic.

https://i.imgur.com/t0Sxs9q.gif

During the zenith days of Aurs, players can attend an event known as The Festival of Souls. You’ll be able to uncover a wide variety of season-specific quests and meet strange, unusual characters that come from all corners of the kingdom. On the surface, the festival is a celebration of remembrance for the souls of friends and family now passed. But beware! Lurking in the shadows, just out of reach of the safety of festival lights, are more unsavory types conducting bloodcurdling business. Who knows, depending on your in-game choices and the factions you align yourself with, one of these individuals could be you?

https://i.imgur.com/rfWB5DN.gif

The season of Aur is not merely about combat, magic, and questing, but also the game’s other notable mechanic of crafting and creation. An assortment of special structures, accessories, and weapon recipes can be crafted during the season, each with its own Aur-flavored twist. Lastly, we would be terrible game developers if we didn’t give the player the Aur season’s recipe they desired most:  the ability to craft their very own pumpkin spice lattes! 

This is just scratching the surface of special in-game activities the player can take advantage of during the Season of Harvest. These key seasons and events are a free permanent addition to the game, the player can experience all of its content while progressing through the main storyline. We look forward to showing you more about this season and others in future blog posts to come! Till then, Happy Halloween from all of us working on Ars Notoria!

notes.title: Ars Notoria Journal #3
notes.content:
Hey everyone!

In the third part of our development journal, we wanted to talk about the combat classes in Ars Notoria. There are six primary weapon types available in the game: Swords, Pistols, Blunt Weapons, Rifles, Polearms, and Hand Mortars.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42814198/8aa1aabc4b271bb0efcb077b18e59c887876f346.png

Each weapon type has a corresponding weapon skill that increases every time your character uses it. After leveling up the weapon skill, you can choose new active abilities for the character or upgrade existing ones.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42814198/b04b9b7ecc2b859f9eb02e4b362fac7120735471.png

There are 12 base abilities, with multiple levels for each weapon skill. Offensive abilities range from combo attacks that allow you to quickly perform a series of strikes to special attacks that can hit multiple enemies at once. Ability trees also offer some defensive options for the characters like Sidesteps, Dodges, Blocking, and Parrying.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42814198/e84a573a81d24592017331929e8895dcfbac20d1.png

Ranged weapons also support alternative firing modes. For example, Pistols have rapid-firing attacks that are especially effective against small and fast-moving enemies and powerful attacks that are great against heavily armored opponents. Rifles can be used to accurately hit targets from long distances or to perform devastating buckshot attacks at a close range. Hand Mortars can shoot mortar rounds that follow arc-shaped trajectories and deal damage in a large radius, or use rockets capable of destroying fortified positions and tough enemies.

Swordsman

https://i.imgur.com/89TH5Ff.gif

Swordsmen are specialists in melee combat and one-on-one skirmishes. They can use a variety of slashing and piercing attacks, as well as strong cleaving strikes that can break through the opponent’s armor. They use Swords and light but sturdy armor that allows them to keep good mobility and excellent offensive capabilities.

Scout

https://i.imgur.com/4gk7H2x.gif

Scout is the fastest of base combat classes, but also the most vulnerable. Scouts use Pistols as their primary weapons and usually wear light armor. They have very high maneuverability and use it to their advantage to attack from behind or employ hit-and-run tactics. Their main defense lies in quickly dodging upcoming attacks and dealing counterattacks that can interrupt the enemy’s offense.

Vanguard

https://i.imgur.com/onotl8C.gif

Vanguards are frontline soldiers equipped with Blunt Weapons and Shields, and wearing medium armor. They have much better defenses than Swordsmen, but their damage output can be slightly lower due to this. Vanguards are especially strong in blocking or parrying enemy attacks and breaking through enemy ranks. Their abilities are well-rounded and allow them to fight proficiently against all types of adversaries.

Marksman

https://i.imgur.com/pICAuHf.gif

Marksman can attack enemies from a much longer range than other classes and have high damage output. They use Rifles and wear medium armor, which allows them to withstand enemies even in close combat when needed. Marksman is a versatile class that has both long-range, high-precision attacks and close-quarter blasts with buckshot.

Lancer

https://i.imgur.com/buGb279.gif

Lancers are melee warriors who utilize Polearms which have a large radius of attack and deal heavy damage. They are especially strong in combat against groups of enemies and weakly protected targets. Lancers are equipped with heavy armor that is very durable and allows them to withstand even the heaviest enemy attacks.

Grenadier

https://i.imgur.com/MxuyN4V.gif

Grenadier is the heaviest of ranged combat classes and the most effective in breaking through enemy fortifications. Their Hand Mortars and heavy armor allow them to stay close to the frontlines and launch devastating mortar and rocket attacks on their opponents. Although they are not as fast as Scouts or as precise as Marksmen, Grenadiers are capable of quickly defeating large groups of enemies or dealing large amounts of damage to armored targets.

In this article, we only covered the base combat classes of Ars Notoria, but each of them also has various specializations that allow you to further customize and improve your characters. Specializations are unique for each in-game faction and grant additional abilities to characters or significantly modify existing ones. We will cover them in more detail in further articles after we introduce the factions.

Thank you a lot for checking this entry in our development journal!

notes.title: Ars Notoria Journal #2
notes.content:
Hey everyone!

In the second entry of our development journal, we wanted to talk about different enemy types you will encounter while exploring the world of Ars Notoria. Various deadly creatures roam the territories of the kingdom and pose a significant threat to its inhabitants.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42814198/1fb46e049ac58ea512004f0a906b5f2c1d7d2dbc.jpg

Enthralled

Enthralled are magic-infused beasts formed by corrupted shards of spiritual energy. They roam the kingdom’s territories, seeking to unleash further death upon the mortal world and corrupt more souls in their wake. These beings are often deformed and mutated to larger sizes due to the unpredictable nature of spiritual corruption.

https://i.imgur.com/lQD3sMX.gif

All Enthralled carry some level of magic, as indicated by their soul auras. A skilled Soul Hunter can read such auras and determine the best way to defeat possessed creatures based on the type of spiritual magic they are corrupted with. There are different types of magic that spirits imbue Enthralled with: from Fire and Ice to Lightning and Poison. Spirits grant unique elemental spells to the controlled beings and also make them much stronger, faster, and more resilient than their normal counterparts.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42814198/ceba84d613df0ade2852ae1a200663a20771bed3.jpg

Aberrations

Creatures that were possessed by stronger spirits and can mutate even further than regular Enthralled are known as Aberrations. Insects that grow larger than most animals, gigantic spiders that prey on humans, and crabs that can split the boat in half with their pincers are examples of such Aberrations.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42814198/421137df5db7c015ec318602f959ed1d030cb387.jpg

Aberrations are more dangerous enemies than Enthralled beasts, and only professionally trained Soul Hunters might stand a chance when fighting against them. Despite being a higher threat in combat, Aberrations are not as common as other spiritually corrupted creatures, and encounters with them are pretty rare.

Therianthropes

Therianthropes are powerful humanoid beings that were possessed by spirits for long periods of time and changed their appearance considerably due to effects of the soul corruption. Some examples of such creatures include Lycanthropes, more commonly known as Werewolves, Arkanthropes or Werebears, and Aroanthropes or Wererats.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42814198/f3d01e35f8ac556e8281e3aebbb2dcf5336743a4.jpg

Therianthropes are the most powerful of the possessed enemies. They are extremely lethal and can easily defeat even a squad of experienced Soul Hunters that venture into their lair. Unlike other enchanted monsters, Therianthropes are much smarter, and they try to avoid contact with humans by often staying far away from settlements and hiding deep in the woods or in remote dungeons.

Undead

The effects of spiritual corruption not only affected the living beings throughout the kingdom but led to the rise of the undead. Spiritual energy filled the remains of ancient soldiers that were buried in numerous tombs, crypts, and ossuaries for centuries and allowed them to move again.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42814198/424412899e0f5c35f4f474c3bf56e86b2f920831.jpg

After spending years on end in their tombs, ancient warriors become frail, and their weapons completely rusted out. But corrupted shards of spiritual energy granted them new magical powers and strengthened their decaying bones, making them formidable foes once again.

Factions

Perhaps the most dangerous enemy of all is not magical beasts, but various factions vying for control over the region. Led by the renowned and mighty warriors, each one having their own ideology and pursuing their goals, they are capable of bringing more destruction and chaos to the kingdom than any of the monsters.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42814198/c306c5645a19c432580507a88bda67804873b508.jpg

We will cover all in-game factions in more detail in the future entries of our development journal. Thank you a lot for checking out this article!

Please feel free to join our Discord channel and follow us on socials.

https://i.imgur.com/Q4PQcha.png
